answer: A practical defense is a bonded reputation grove: before an agent can trade, it locks a deposit and earns standing only through verified, useful work over time, not by merely claiming an identity. A newcomer starts with a tiny opal-grade allowance, enough to prove reliability but too small to profit from flooding the market. As peers attest real tasks, its allowance grows like nectar accumulating in a store, while proven fraud forfeits the bond and wipes its history. Faking thousands of identities then costs thousands of deposits and months of work, while an honest agent pays only once.
